2.05.betting_forecast: 2/7 Runman, 11/2 Vitality, 14/1 Get Outta Here, Hattie's Comet, 20/1 Fizzy Bear, 25/1 Mick The Hat, Thomas Picton, 66/1 Pureis
2.05.spotlight_verdict: A novice with no depth and it will be disappointing should RUNMAN not win it well en route to bigger and better things. Vitality is the clear danger after a mildly promising debut on the AW.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: Modest fifth at Kempton before finishing just ahead of Thomas Picton when both were down the field at Newbury ten days ago.
Beaten in the region of 7l at Deauville (7f) and Kempton (1m); likely to be seen in a better light when handicapping.
62,000gns yearling out of a 7f/1m winner (Listed; RPR 100) and half-sister to French winners Spherical (7f) and I Am Incredible (5.5f); best watched unless the betting suggests otherwise.
Bought for £1,800 after one run for Andre Fabre; beaten 28l in one run over hurdles for Jamie Snowden and was last at Yarmouth on recent stable debut (1m).
Handicaps could beckon after this following down-the-field runs on the AW (at about 1m; 16-1/80-1).
Bumper winner but well beaten in two 1m races on the Kempton AW and unlikely to be winning this.

Half-brother to the classy 1m-1m2f performer Running Lion and this colt was nicely on top late on in a useful 1m novice at Salisbury in October; could easily outclass this opposition and progress to better things.
65,000euros yearling; 66-1 when 18th of 25 in a 1m Newbury maiden ten days ago; this race has far less depth.
Went down by 3l in a five-runner 1m Southwell maiden (16-1) after making the running; a 3yo filly taking on the males but could prove the main threat to Runman.

2.40.betting_forecast: 4/9 New Zealand, 100/30 Saxon Street, 8/1 Balzac, 16/1 Rebel Rocker, 33/1 Menzies, Pearl River.
2.40.spotlight_verdict: This race has been anything but a shoo-in for Aidan O'Brien in recent years but NEW ZEALAND still makes most appeal on the bare form, with guesswork involved regarding rivals who have kept lower profiles. Although no whirlwind as a juvenile, New Zealand ran to a useful level in a Group 3 at Newmarket in the autumn and he was aiming high in a Group 1 in France later. The race's history suggests a big step forward is possible for some and the Gosdens' runner Saxon Street is a likely candidate who can provide the most danger. Balzac and Rebel Rocker are others with more to come this year.[Emily Weber]

horses.spotlight_comment: Winning siblings include Claymore, a Group 3 winner at 1m2f for this yard; lots to like about his persevering third of seven in a good 1m Newmarket maiden (22-1; ridden by 7lb claimer) on debut but he didn't need any more than that form when making all on Kempton AW (1m) this month; Derby entry who should make a better 3yo but how much better will be clearer after today.

One sibling was a Graded winner at 1m3f and 1m1f in US; took a step forward from 7f debut on Kempton AW when making the running and not for catching over 1m there in February; had more to do under a penalty at Southwell since and he fell short so now relies on big improvement for the step up in trip.
horses.breeding: ch c Australia - Voice Of Truth

horses.spotlight_comment: By Frankel; dam won the Group 3 Albany (6f) as 2yo and bred Group-placed Agenda (1m4f) for this yard; clung on for 7f maiden win at the Curragh on second start but was a better horse in the autumn, not having much to race against when involved in a scramble for second in a Group 3 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) then bogged down by the class rise and/or very soft ground in the Group 1 Criterium International at Saint-Cloud; likely to do better as a 3yo over this longer trip; good chance with sights lowered.

All five races on good or slower; middling form on first three starts but was all the better for the step up to 1m2f on final two runs and his stamina was much in evidence when forging clear in a Nottingham handicap (good to soft), despite running green; needs to have come on a ton over the winter to play a part and the track and good to firm ground are other queries.

Derby entry; nibbled at in the market for 1m debut on Kempton AW in November where he made a good impression with the way he made up ground to win quite convincingly; his rivals had some limitations though and although this one should improve he is asked a big question today.

170,000euros yearling; unraced dam's winning siblings include Raheen House (1m5f; Group 3) and Shraaoh (Australian 2m Group 1); a warm order for Chelmsford AW debut (1m) in December and although workmanlike rather than impressive in beating rivals who mostly look handicappers in the making, he did finish with purpose; should leave that form well behind over a more suitable trip for yard that's won five of the last ten runnings; entered in the Dante and the Derby.

3.15.betting_forecast: 11/4 Dangerman, 4/1 Sallaal, 9/2 Rathgar, 6/1 Aurel, 13/2 Asmen Warrior, 7/1 Duke's Command, 8/1 Parlando.
3.15.spotlight_verdict: The 4yo DANGERMAN could be just the type of Gosden runner to keep on improving this season and he earns the vote on his reappearance. Sallaal is another who should be set for a good campaign and he is second choice ahead of recent Newbury winner Rathgar, who was second in this last year.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Runner-up last July-October on three of his first four starts for this yard and he again finished second on this month's reappearance at Thirsk (1m4f, good), albeit no match for the winner; he could build on that latest effort and is not discounted.
horses.breeding: ch g Saxon Warrior - Fair Sailing

horses.spotlight_comment: Absent since midfield finish in Golden Gates Handicap at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) last June; gelded since; however, he was 2-3 previously, the wins coming in a maiden at Kempton (1m, AW) and a novice at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm), and he may well have more to offer for his respected trainer.

Won two in a row at Sandown (1m2f, good) last summer when these blinkers went on and third there (1m2f, soft) next time; appeared unsuited by the step up to 1m4f at Newmarket in October; this lightly raced 4yo is in excellent hands and could rediscover his progressive ways with a big run today.

Won at Lingfield (AW) in December on first crack at 1m2f and raced wide when sixth of 14 at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last month; this two-time turf winner remains unexposed at today's trip and is not ruled out.

Two AW wins in December and returned to turf with 3l third of eight at Pontefract (1m2f, good) last Tuesday; might not be far away but there's a suspicion that this exposed 7yo might find a few too good; cheekpieces go on.

Beat 13 rivals to win at Newbury (1m2f, good) ten days ago on his second start back from some time off; back up 4lb but he's just 1lb higher than when second in this last year and he's a solid contender.
horses.breeding: ch g Ulysses - Why We Dream

horses.spotlight_comment: Made it three wins from his first four starts when scoring on handicap debut at Hamilton (8.3f, good) last July; his progress stalled in two Listed races subsequently but this lightly raced 4yo has been gelded since and the return to better ground could be a positive, along with the step up in trip; retains potential for a top trainer who won this in 2018 and 2019; respected.

3.50.betting_forecast: 7/4 Topteam, 11/4 Sing Us A Song, 4/1 Asgard's Captain, 9/2 Night Breeze, 8/1 Nunc Est Bibendum.
3.50.spotlight_verdict: Just the five for this year's Great Met but they include last year's winner Asgard's Captain (second choice) who looks sure to go well. Unexposed Sing Us A Song is also respected on his comeback but the vote goes to Andrew Balding's TOPTEAM (nap), who has a lovely way of going about his business and can register win number four on turf.[Richard Russell]

horses.spotlight_comment: Last year's winner (good) who ran well in two other appearances over C&D; did well to win at York (1m4f, good to firm) under John Egan in August and arrives here fit after three creditable efforts at Meydan; firm contender.
horses.breeding: b g Make Believe - Twiggy's Girl

horses.spotlight_comment: Not disgraced in last year's Northern Dancer over C&D (good; likely softer) on sole start here; also won twice at Ascot (good to firm) last term; back to form on last two starts, latterly when beaten 2l at Musselburgh (also 1m4f, good) on Sunday; should make his presence felt.
horses.breeding: b g New Approach - Right Direction

horses.spotlight_comment: Ex-Irish mare who secured an AW hat-trick once upped to 2m across December and January but suffered odds-on reversal when dropped to 1m6f in bid for the four-timer; drops further in trip returned to turf (had form on grass in Ireland) on this first start for three months; others more persuasive.

Won heavy-ground Goodwood maiden at two and it was a convincing success on last year's reappearance/handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good) one year ago; disappointed at Royal Ascot and Glorious Goodwood subsequently but had been gelded when back on the scoresheet at Haydock (1m6f, good to soft) in September; drops in trip for this comeback but not fully exposed.

Really likeable sort who scored three times on good ground (1m2f/1m4f) last term, twice coming out on top in tight finishes; gelded before again showing a fine attitude to pick up Kempton handicap (1m4f, AW) on his reappearance three weeks ago; likely won't go down without a fight for his ever-growing fan club.
horses.breeding: b g Oasis Dream - Countess De Vega

4.23.betting_forecast: 2/1 Timber Twelve, 5/2 Montague Menace, 11/4 On Message, 5/1 Terranoble, 14/1 Assaranca, 25/1 Mayaada.
4.23.spotlight_verdict: Four of these are making their handicap debuts and the winner is likely to come from that quartet. Unbeaten Timber Twelve (second choice) must be considered but the vote goes to Ralph Beckett's filly ON MESSAGE, who holds some flashy future entries and could be in for a good year. Montague Menace and Terranoble also carry potential into this sphere.[Richard Russell]

horses.spotlight_comment: Off the mark on her eighth start as a juvenile when landing Nottingham nursery (good, made all) over this trip in October; not disgraced in Listed company next time but weakened over 1m2f (good to soft) on her reappearance one month ago; might do better back at this distance with the run behind her.

Busy as a juvenile when her nine runs yielded one win; that did come here (7f, good) in August but was quiet on last two starts and virtually tailed off on last month's AW comeback; return to this venue might help, and a handicapping case can be made, but otherwise has plenty to prove.
horses.breeding: b f Phoenix Of Spain - Young Special

horses.spotlight_comment: Gelded ahead of his AW debut when readily landing Lingfield maiden (7f) on last month's return; will probably need more on this switch back to turf/handicap debut but it's still early days and he warrants consideration.
horses.breeding: b g Mehmas - Tower Of Pisa

horses.spotlight_comment: Promise on first two starts (good to firm/soft) and she made all on AW debut at Wolverhampton (7f) in October; should do better at this trip and beyond (holds Oaks and Irish Oaks entries) this term; interesting on her reappearance and handicap debut.

All starts around 1m on AW; only made his debut in December but that was an eyecatching effort and he improved on third start to land Wolverhampton novice in January; potential to do better again on this turf/handicap debut.

Overcame a wide stall when springing 28-1 surprise at Kempton in September and kept unbeaten record when defying a penalty on his return at Southwell (also 1m, AW) five weeks ago; will likely be going up in trip soon enough but brings plenty of potential to this turf/handicap debut.

4.58.betting_forecast: 9/4 Tribal Rhythm, 7/2 Mr Baloo, 9/2 Kaleido, 7/1 Shafdar, 10/1 Amused, Carnival Day, 14/1 Sweet Reward, 16/1 Tronido, 20/1
4.58.spotlight_verdict: Unexposed pair Kaleido and Shafdar are candidates to step forward but this can be fought out by last year's winner Tribal Rhythm and MR BALOO. The former looked unlucky on his return earlier this month but preference is for Richard Hannon's 5yo, who retains handicapping scope and can go 2-2 in cheekpieces.[Richard Russell]

horses.spotlight_comment: Ex-French gelding who was unraced at two; made all to land Vichy claimer (very soft) in August and went mighty close for this yard in Leicester seller (good) in October; 25-1 and raced wide before solid fifth of 12 at Kempton (also 7f, AW) when last seen in December; cheekpieces enlisted for second go at this sort of trip and he's not ruled out on return.
horses.breeding: b g No Nay Never - Happy Face

horses.spotlight_comment: Respectable fourth in the Great Metropolitan on last year's card; one win last year but it did come here in July and he was a respectable second at this track (also 1m2f, good to soft; has won on good) in September; below par over 1m on his final start in October and this trip again asks a question; market might help ahead of his comeback.
horses.breeding: b g Invincible Spirit - Mardie Gras

horses.spotlight_comment: Placed on soft and fast ground in his first three maidens (7f/1m) before landing the odds with comfortable win at Yarmouth (7f, good) in July; made favourite for handicap debut but weakened to finish ninth at Glorious Goodwood (1m, heavy; Knights Gold third) a fortnight later; bought for 21,000gns in October and subsequently gelded; retains plenty of potential ahead of this seasonal/stable debut.

Insole Rossa Ryan 20-1 84 84 97 Five handicap wins (7f to 1m; four in a hood) in a productive 2025, including on a fast surface, and he looked unlucky when third of 15 at Glorious Goodwood (1m, heavy; Kaleido ninth) in July; probably needed reappearance in March and likely didn't stay 1m2f when never competitive three weeks later; this mark demands a return to his best, though.
horses.breeding: b g Dark Angel - Samira Gold

horses.spotlight_comment: 7f nursery winner here (good; has won on good to firm) in 2023; landed seventh AW win when scoring at Lingfield (1m; first-time cheekpieces, retained) a fortnight ago; has won off higher marks than this and must be considered on his return to turf.

Completed a hat-trick over 7f/1m on good/good to firm across May and June last year; form tailed off markedly from August onwards but he returns just 2lb above his last winning mark; market support would bring him into the picture.

All starts on AW for this yard and he justified cramped odds when easily landing four-runner Chelmsford maiden (1m) in February; promising handicap debut when second over that C&D the following month and can be excused a lesser effort in highly competitive Good Friday event three weeks later; unexposed, particularly on this surface, and he warrants consideration.

Seven wins include five off higher marks than this and one at this track (1m2f, good to soft; has won on good) in 2023; this trip might be on the short side but he went close on his reappearance in 2024 (1m2f) and scored off 2lb higher on his comeback last term (1m2f); not readily dismissed.

Returned from seven months off to win this race from off the pace last year; couldn't build on that in four subsequent starts last season but was back down to that winning mark when slightly unlucky second at Bath (1m, also good) on his resumption three weeks ago; of firm interest.

Four-time winner who won at Sandown in August and followed up by 6l over C&D (soft; acts on good) in September; just 2lb above that latter winning mark but there hasn't been much encouragement in three AW starts this term.
